summaryEn: Teaches you to describe a job with a relative clause.
Teaches you to describe a path through education with infinitive phrases of intention and purpose.
Teaches you to ask about specialist details you do not know, with indirect questions.
Teaches you to describe the work done at an office in passive sentences.
Teaches you to describe decisions taken in the past with the past form of the passive.
Teaches you to put a suggestion and a request politely, in the subjunctive.
Teaches you to tell the story of a job search in layers of the past.
Teaches you to present figures in a balanced way with paired conjunctions.
Teaches you to state the aim of a decision with a damit clause.
Teaches you to talk about job satisfaction with fixed-preposition verbs.
Teaches you to describe a period in the past with the conjunction als.
Teaches you to ask what you do not know at an official agency, with indirect questions.
Teaches you to compare languages and levels of language.
Teaches you to discuss both sides of a social question with paired conjunctions.
Teaches you to state an opinion and a doubt in a subordinate clause.
Teaches you to describe court proceedings with the past form of the passive.
Teaches you to describe an event you saw with relative clauses.
Teaches you to understand rules and limits in passive sentences.
Teaches you to talk about a sensitive subject while stating a reservation.
Teaches you to state the aim of an action with a damit clause.
Teaches you to describe a venue and an event with relative clauses after a preposition.
Teaches you to describe a book and its author with relative clauses.
Teaches you to describe a celebration in order, with conjunctions of time.
Teaches you to state an intention and to give advice with an infinitive phrase.
Teaches you to describe what happened in a match with the past form of the passive.
Teaches you to describe a one-off day in the past with the conjunction als.
Teaches you to compare the weather and the shape of the land.
Teaches you to describe an animal with dative relative clauses.
Teaches you the polite patterns of suggestion and request in the subjunctive, while making plans.
Teaches you to look back on the road traveled and to describe the next step with paired conjunctions.
Teaches you to open a presentation and to set out the plan in the nominal style of institutions.
Teaches you to describe figures and trends with the passive perfect.
Teaches you to steer a meeting in the subjunctive and to minute a decision.
Teaches you to turn what was said into the language of minutes, in reported speech.
Teaches you to understand, postpone and clarify the questions after a presentation.
Teaches you to make short, non-committal work small talk with polite patterns.
Teaches you to hand out tasks and to say what is feasible, with the stand-ins for the passive.
Teaches you to make a conditional promise with sofern and es sei denn.
Teaches you to set out the rules of a working arrangement in the nominal style of institutions.
Teaches you to meet people at a conference, giving reason and time with genitive prepositions.
Teaches you to negotiate price and terms in the subjunctive, without closing the door.
Teaches you to build the nominal, distanced language of a formal letter of complaint.
Teaches you to describe a fault and to ask for a fix, with the stand-ins for the passive.
Teaches you to state the cause of the damage and your claim, with genitive prepositions.
Teaches you to build sentences of concession and compromise with two-part conjunctions.
Teaches you to calm an angry caller with understanding and the subjunctive.
Teaches you to give notice, with the language of periods, confirmation and withdrawal.
Teaches you to settle a dispute with a neighbor with conditional conjunctions, without going to the management.
Teaches you to describe a recurring fault in the past passive and to demand a replacement.
Teaches you to give criticism in order: observation, suggestion, question.
